rules.statement: When evicting a cache whose entries are built from another cache, clear the source cache first and await it before clearing the derived cache; don't run both clears fire-and-forget or in reverse order.
rules.why: A derived entry built between the two clears would be rebuilt from a stale source entry and serve stale settings until it expires.
rules.check: Look for cache-invalidation code that clears a derived cache before its source, or starts both clears without awaiting them in dependency order.

rules.statement: When one change evicts several related caches one after another, isolate each eviction (separate try/catch that logs, or the dependent eviction in a `finally`) so that a failed eviction doesn't skip the others.
rules.why: If the first eviction throws, the dependent entries stay cached with stale data until their lifetime expires.
rules.check: Look for back-to-back cache `RemoveAsync`/clear calls with no isolation between them, where an exception from the first would skip the second.

rules.statement: When a recovery or fallback operation runs after a failure, don't let an exception from the recovery replace the original exception; rethrow the original with the recovery failure attached (for example via `ExceptionDispatchInfo` or an `AggregateException`).
rules.why: Otherwise the logs show the secondary failure instead of the one that caused it, and nothing logged the original before the recovery ran.
rules.check: Look for catch blocks that call another fallible operation (such as a re-read after a failed insert) without a try around it that keeps the original exception.

rules.statement: After a mechanical rename or search-and-replace sweep, check the doc comments and prose it touched for unrelated words that were also replaced, including matches that span a line break.
rules.why: A blind replacement can make public IntelliSense text name an entity that doesn't exist, contradicting the surrounding docs.
rules.check: In rename diffs, read the changed doc-comment lines for replaced terms that no longer make sense in context, such as compound terms altered by mistake.

rules.statement: A `cref` or type name in a member's XML doc must name the type the member actually returns or uses, not a sibling type.
rules.why: A public API doc that points at the wrong type misleads readers.
rules.check: Compare `<see cref>` targets in property and method summaries with the declared return and parameter types, especially on lines the diff edits.

rules.statement: Remove constructor-injected dependencies that the class stores but never reads.
rules.why: A dead dependency makes readers check it for nothing and makes DI resolve a service for nothing.
rules.check: Look for constructor parameters or properties (such as a `TimeProvider` carried over from copied code) that no member of the class reads.

rules.statement: Don't report a missing `SectionName` constant on an options type that is a subsection of a parent options type and is bound through the parent's `SectionName`.
rules.why: Subsection options are bound as part of their parent, so only the root options type needs its own section-name constant.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether the options type is a property of a parent options class that has its own `SectionName` and is bound as a unit.

rules.statement: Don't report a configuration section rename as a violation of the no-rename-in-refactor rule when an ADR records the rename as part of an intended model change under the pre-release posture (renamed outright with no alias) and every config file, program and chart in the repository uses the new name.
rules.why: In the pre-release family, ADRs call for renaming configuration sections outright when the model changes, rather than keeping aliases.
rules.check: Before reporting, look for an ADR that names the new section, and check that appsettings files, host programs, charts and docs all use the new name.

rules.statement: Don't report that paired management operations check whether a tenant is served differently when one acts through the tenant's runtime (so it materializes the tenant and refuses a tenant that isn't served) and the other changes stored configuration only.
rules.why: A route that acts through a tenant's runtime must materialize the tenant before it writes, while stored configuration stays manageable for a disabled tenant.
rules.check: Before reporting, see whether each operation touches runtime state (such as ending sessions) or only persisted configuration.

rules.statement: Don't report an `as object` cast that passes a `data-*` attribute (such as a test id) into MUI's typed `slotProps`, because those slot prop types don't declare `data-*` attributes.
rules.why: Without the cast the attribute can't reach the typed input slot props.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether the cast object only adds `data-*` attributes to an MUI slot.
